extracted.intended_audience: intermediate improvisers (students who have completed Magnet Level Two or equivalent) seeking advanced longform ensemble skills
extracted.subtask_description: A Level Three improv class focused on advanced scene work and ensemble play for performers aiming to master longform techniques, group games, and collaborative scene success. Students should already have Magnet Level Two or equivalent experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced scene work
rubrics_metrics.description: This class is all about advanced scene work and learning how to play in an ensemble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on higher-level scene construction, sustaining scenes over time, and making choices that develop the scene rather than stopping it. Exercises and practice will center on complex scene dynamics appropriate to advanced students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble play / Group Mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to play in an ensemble; emphasis on 'Group Mind!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop collective awareness and responsiveness so the group functions as a coherent unit. Prioritize ensemble cohesion and shared objectives over individual spotlighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightening others' choices
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to master any longform you need to know how to heighten other people’s choices as well as your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and amplify partners' offers instead of negating them; build on established bits and raise the stakes or specificity to move scenes forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate listening
rubrics_metrics.description: You will become the ultimate listener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate deep, active listening to notice and act on subtle offers, callbacks, and opportunities from teammates; listening drives truthful reactions and strong ensemble work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-tasking as a performer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage multiple scene elements (space, relationships, status, callbacks) simultaneously without losing clarity; balance attention between personal choices and group developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team player without losing your voice
rubrics_metrics.description: You will become a team player without losing your own voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribute to the ensemble while maintaining distinctive, interesting choices; avoid subsuming individuality entirely—bring personal creativity in service of the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playing group games
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to play group games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice structures and formats for multi-player scenes and games that require coordination, timing, and shared rules; understand how to enter and exit group games smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating fun, successful scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to play scenes that are fun and actually succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for scenes that deliver comedic payoff and narrative satisfaction; use heightening, listening, and ensemble tools to produce scenes that land with audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: Magnet Level Two or equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerequisite: Magnet Level Two or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should have completed the prior level or possess comparable longform/improv experience to handle advanced material in this class.
